$comment: Presentation profiles (buildout W1.10). The ontology profile (profiles/) decides WHICH kinds exist; a portal template decides HOW a brain is displayed: the nav grouping and order, the front door's framing, the default retrieval resolution, and which kinds it foregrounds. Selected in client.config.json `portal.template`. A template is a VIEW over the pages an instance registers — it orders and groups registered pages and never invents one; a registered page a template does not list falls under its own `group` after the template's groups. Switching templates changes the front door and nav with no page edits. Page-sets (#203): a registered page carrying `requires: <overlay>` is registered only when profile.overlays selects that overlay, so a template's engagement-only group (Delivery, Plan) is empty and hidden in a brain without the engagement overlay. A template may also declare `excludes` (page-sets it never shows) or `includes` (the only page-sets it shows); both narrow the registered pages and neither adds one. Each template carries `assistantCopy` (portal title, chat greeting and placeholder, assistant identity and audience, with {name}/{domain}/{scope} placeholders): `make init` stamps the selected template's copy into client.config.json, so prompt defaults follow the brain's kind rather than living as literals (#206/#200). Purpose homes (#397) declare presentation-only actions, reader-visible record sections, and suggested questions. They never grant access, enable features, or add routes.
